bug_semantics: Penpot MCP automatically started an Express ReplServer whose POST /execute route accepted an unauthenticated JSON code string and sent it through PluginBridge as an ExecuteCodePluginTask; the plugin handler evaluated that string with new Function in a context exposing the Penpot API, storage, console, and PenpotUtils. ReplServer called app.listen(this.port) without a host, so Node/Express listened on all interfaces rather than loopback. Consequently, an unauthenticated adjacent-network peer that could reach port 4403 could cause arbitrary JavaScript execution in the connected Penpot plugin context.
flaw_origin: Upstream penpot/penpot-mcp commit 8552bb4183fc1479c8436c1ccec2868ea221d498 ('Add REPL server') introduced the entire ReplServer, the unauthenticated /execute sink, the hostless app.listen(this.port), and automatic startup from PenpotMcpServer in one commit. The later penpot/penpot aggregate import 880b9b61c41f977f4ddf8463ab6ab62194acb077 copied upstream snapshot fcfa67e908fc54e23a3a3543dee432472dc90c5d; it did not originate the flaw.
ai_marker: absent — the raw BIC commit object names human author Dominik Jain <dominik.jain@outlook.com> and human committer Dominik Jain <dominik.jain@oraios-ai.de>; its complete message is only 'Add REPL server' and has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI-assistance trailer. The corporate string 'ai' in the committer email domain is not a commit-object AI authorship marker.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/penpot/penpot/security/advisories/GHSA-22qr-rp27-j9wm identifies mcp/packages/server/src/ReplServer.ts: the unauthenticated POST /execute route and listen(this.port) default-all-interfaces binding, with patched version 2.15.0.

In a read-only full-history checkout of upstream https://github.com/penpot/penpot-mcp, git log --reverse -S'this.app.listen(this.port)' -- mcp-server/src/ReplServer.ts and the parallel -S'this.app.post("/execute"' search both return 8552bb4183fc1479c8436c1ccec2868ea221d498 as the first commit. Its diff adds ReplServer.ts from /dev/null, including both the /execute route and app.listen(this.port), and wires new ReplServer(this.pluginBridge) into PenpotMcpServer startup.

Direct parent-tree verification: git cat-file -e 8552bb4183fc1479c8436c1ccec2868ea221d498^:mcp-server/src/ReplServer.ts fails because the path does not exist; git diff-tree reports ReplServer.ts as A. The raw commit object gives immediate parent ad771ee92fbbf36b2d3b515e1a16e551a39cc986. Thus the vulnerable server, route, and binding are absent from the immediate parent.

Import decomposition: penpot commit 880b9b61c41f977f4ddf8463ab6ab62194acb077 explicitly records 'Original repository: https://github.com/penpot/penpot-mcp' and 'Imported commit: fcfa67e908fc54e23a3a3543dee432472dc90c5d'. Upstream merge-base --is-ancestor proves 8552bb4183fc1479c8436c1ccec2868ea221d498 is an ancestor of fcfa67e908fc54e23a3a3543dee432472dc90c5d. The upstream fcfa ReplServer blob and monorepo 880b9 ReplServer blob have the identical Git object ID 978f0e2ea4f97fcc9d4836c4f07b2bb31a89bcd9, making 8552bb4 the reconstructable smallest BIC rather than the 30,118-line import aggregate.

Attack-path source at imported commit 880b9b61c41f977f4ddf8463ab6ab62194acb077 shows ExecuteCodePluginTask creates task type executeCode, while ExecuteCodeTaskHandler evaluates task.params.code using new Function with penpot, storage, console, and PenpotUtils in scope. ReplServer passes the unauthenticated request body directly into that task.

Fix verification: direct one-parent commit 798ee46b4a84ee6dfc756b001f33acbe0280d62f (parent 697a825d76c5d7bd8b28a57b0d4be049a91f2455) adds a host parameter defaulting to localhost, forwards PenpotMcpServer.this.host, and changes app.listen(this.port, callback) to app.listen(this.port, this.host, callback). Its commit message explicitly describes the unauthenticated-RCE exposure and contains the direct source fix, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are the same commit.

Version boundary: integration commit 880b9b61c41f977f4ddf8463ab6ab62194acb077 is absent from every 2.13.x tag but is contained by 2.14.0 commit 13b5c96a429070b959d5cd6e0082112ce6724efc and all queried 2.14.x tags; fix 798ee46b4a84ee6dfc756b001f33acbe0280d62f is contained by no 2.14.x tag, but is contained by patched 2.15.0 tag commit bd3ca6f8e56869a18731544099c35bd4ab2824b6. This matches the advisory's <2.15.0 vulnerable / 2.15.0 patched boundary for releases carrying MCP.

BIC-only AI inspection: git show -s --format=raw 8552bb4183fc1479c8436c1ccec2868ea221d498 shows author and committer Dominik Jain and no trailers or AI/bot marker in the commit message. No PR-body, branch-name, import-commit, later-change, or fix-commit signal was used for attribution.
reasoning: The causal unit is the upstream Add REPL server commit, not Penpot's later bulk import. Commit 8552bb4 simultaneously made a dangerous evaluator reachable through an unauthenticated HTTP route and exposed that route beyond loopback by omitting the listen host. Its immediate parent has no ReplServer file, and content-addressed blob equality plus the import commit's recorded upstream SHA reconstructs how that exact vulnerable implementation entered penpot/penpot. Later upstream edits moved the HTML, added REPL history, and standardized configuration without originating the vulnerable route/binding. The monorepo import first reached the 2.14 release series; 798ee46 directly constrained ReplServer to the configured host, localhost by default, and is present in 2.15.0 but no 2.14.x tag. Finally, the only permitted attribution source—the raw 8552bb4 commit object—contains a human author/committer and no AI marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
